reply_text:
All 114 branches and both pin tags are now on the private fork, and every one matches its local copy. Next I'm copying the notes from `/tmp` into `/home/joe` and checking for uncommitted work.The notes snapshot is pushed. Checking that the remote branch matches, then removing the temporary worktree.㊥ (backups) Everything is now copied into `/home/joe` and pushed to the private GitHub forks. All 114 branches of the mfuton repo and the two pin tags are on `tothedarktowercame/mfuton-share`. I checked that every one matches its local copy. The `/tmp` notes are also on that fork, as a separate branch.

㊢ (what went where)
- **Committed code:** this was already safe in `/home/joe`. Every `/tmp/mfs-*` worktree and the Lisp worktrees store their commits in `~/code/mfuton-share/.git`. The branches had only to be pushed: 19 were on the fork before, 114 are now.
- **The notes in `/tmp/pyreg`:** the overnight plan, the probe log, the packets and the new review note. They're copied to `~/mfuton-notes/pyreg`, with the review also at `~/mfuton-notes/TN-lean-continued-port-review.md`.
  - They're also committed to a fork branch of their own, `notes/claude-4-pyreg` (`8152e86`). It has no shared history with the code, so it can't be merged into it by mistake.
  - I left out one 32 MB folder of generated cache under `domain/`.
- **Uncommitted edits:** nine checkouts had changes nobody has committed. I saved each one as a patch in `~/mfuton-notes/uncommitted-2026-10-03/`, which is also on the notes branch, and left the checkouts untouched. Six are old `/tmp/mfs-*` scratch worktrees. The other three:
  - the Lisp checkout, including codex-18's in-progress `runtime.lisp` and the edit to the Python file;
  - the binding repo, an edit to `ParserSource.lean`;
  - `/tmp/mfs-revert-3ef`, 14 changed files.
- **The binding repo:** it was already up to date on its fork, `tothedarktowercame/mfuton-linux-binding`.

㊟ (what isn't covered) `/tmp/mfs-venv` and the generated caches under each worktree's `data/tmp` aren't backed up. They can be rebuilt, though a cold rebuild takes a while. Rob's repository (`origin`) still has pushing disabled, and I didn't touch it.

㊣ (pausing the transpiler) Agreed. While it's paused, codex-18 is the only one editing `runtime.lisp`, so the collisions stop. If codex-18 keeps going, the stubbing proposal in the note would get it past `argparse` sooner than porting it would.

(what it covers)
- **codex-17:** keep all of the integration work, which is at 20 of the 110. Two flaws: the merge `f5d4594` went in without a probe of its own, and the test commit `00e5c04` dropped an assertion.
